source_text: Si haec, inquam, cuncta in Dei imaginem primi hominis invexit iniquitas, manifestum est nimis esse imbecillam Christi gratiam in suis muneri bus, quae nihil, quod his tot trabalibus malis mederetur, invenit; aut si invenit, affirma. Singula enim nunc singulis conferamus. Si Adam praeter voluntatis opera ipsius naturae instituta subvertit, nihil debuit magis Christus quam ea, quae ab illo fuerant elisa, reparare his videlicet vestigiis, quibus ille subruerat.
pass_a_gloss: If these things, I say, all the iniquity of the first human being brought in upon the image of God, it is manifest that Christ's grace is too weak in its gifts, which has found nothing that would heal these so many beam-like evils; or if it has found it, affirm it. For let us now confer singles with singles. If Adam besides the works of will overturned the ordinances of nature itself, Christ ought nothing more than to repair those things which had been struck down by him, by these footprints namely by which that one had undermined.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: —if, I say, the first man’s wickedness inflicted all this on God’s image, Christ’s grace is plainly very weak in its gifts, since it has found nothing to remedy so many massive evils. Or if it has found a remedy, state it. Let us now compare each point individually. If Adam overturned the institutions of nature itself, beyond the acts of his will, Christ should above all have repaired what Adam had shattered, following the very tracks along which Adam had destroyed it.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
